newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai sugar crushing speeds up, yield improves.
newsitem.headline: Thai sugar crushing speeds up, yield improves.

text.p: Thai sugar crushing sped up as more mills started operations and sugar yields edged up from last week, an industry ministry source said on Tuesday.
A total of 28 sugar mills were now in operation compared with 19 as of December 10, the source told Reuters.

Data gathered as of December 15 showed that 1.52 million tonnes of sugarcane had been crushed to produce 105,402 tonnes of raw and white sugar compared with 839,782 tonnes of sugarcane and 57,004 tonnes of sugar last week.
Yields also rose to 69.26 kg of sugar per tonne of sugarcane tonnes from 67.88 a week earlier.
"We expect the yield to rise to at least 103 kg at the end of the crushing season," the source said.
The Thai sugar cane crushing season normally starts in November and ends in late May or early June.
This year the crushing was scheduled to start on November 5 but many mills in the northeast, the first region to start operations, delayed work.
